title: The Promises and Pitfalls of LLM Annotations in Dataset Labeling: a Case Study on Media Bias Detection

model.params_source: assumed (paper silent on decoding parameters; resolution plan fixes temperature 0)

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: BABE train/development combined set = the authors' 75% training split (3,121 sentences; the 1,000-sentence test split is excluded)
task.approximation: the paper's 'openai/gpt-4-turbo' alias is resolved to the 2024-04-09 snapshot by rule (run date not given)

items.source: mediabiasgroup/BABE (train 3,121 / test 1,000; fields text, outlet, label, topic, news_link, biased_words, uuid, type, label_opinion)
items.license: unknown (no license field on the dataset card)
items.hf_verified: Hub parquet default/train: 3,121 rows; columns text, news_link, label (int: 1 = 1740, 0 = 1381), outlet, topic, type, label_opinion, biased_words, uuid

prompt.system: You are an expert in media bias.
prompt.user_template:
Instruction: '{sentence}'
Classify the sentence above as BIASED or NOT BIASED.
Output: Let's think step by step.
prompt.verbatim: full (pseudo-code loop over examples dropped for the zero-shot variant; '[SENTENCE]' slot turned into a placeholder)

placeholders_prose.sentence: items.text (the target sentence; the example loop of Table 8 is empty in the 0-shot setting)

output.postprocess: the greedy regex returns the LAST standalone 'BIASED' / 'NOT BIASED' in the reply (the negative lookbehind prevents matching the tail of 'NOT BIASED'); gold 1/0 mapped to the same strings by items.label_map; the runner compares case-insensitively
output.parse_prose: regex 'The answer is\s*(NOT BIASED|BIASED)' (case-insensitive, last match); fallback: last occurrence of 'NOT BIASED' / 'BIASED' in the reply

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Matthews correlation coefficient between predicted (1 = biased) and gold label over the 3,121 sentences
metric.original_location: Table 1, row GPT-4 Turbo, column '0-shot + sys prompt'

notes: Chain-of-thought replies (~100 tokens) make the call ~ $0.01. The '0-shot Exp' column (0.697) adds a GPT-4-written explanation per example and is not covered here. || [hooks_4 2026-09-07] hook computes the Matthews correlation coefficient.
hook: harness/tierb/hooks/W4411112894.py: parse (LAST 'The answer is <LABEL>', fallback last standalone label), score (MCC, BIASED positive; unparsable = NOT BIASED; no per-item list)
